correctness.rationale: Greedy arches show a shortest linear k-universal word has k consecutive alphabet permutation blocks and length qk. Circular marked words are a union of q cut-phase sets. In an intersection of t phases with cyclic offsets g_i, the segment symbol sets in all k blocks are identical, giving q! (Π g_i!)^(k-1) words per selected subset. Each t-subset counted t times by its rooted q-gap composition and q starting residues, giving coefficient q/t. Equal symbol counts imply any period is q e with e|k. Burnside fixed words under rotations are repeated shorter circular universal words, yielding the totient and Möbius divisor sums. Direct independent enumeration generated all word rotations for (q,k)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2), finding marked/necklace pairs (6,2),(14,3),(78,14).
